summary: Certificate-bound access token thumbprint mismatch after client cert rotation blocks admin API in private deployment
description: Issue summary: After rotating the client mTLS certificate used for IdP token binding, FinWave reports that all admin-console and admin API calls return 401/403. Impact: Admin operators cannot manage role bindings or start rollouts. No user-facing generation impact reported yet, but administrative operations are blocked which prevents remediation of other issues.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer rotates client certificate used for device-bound access tokens in their IdP (Azure AD Enterprise App configured for certificate-bound access).

2) IdP issues access tokens containing 'cnf' claim with x5t#S256 thumbprint referencing the new cert, but some tokens in the customer's environment continue to present the new cert while the auth-proxy validates against an old thumbprint cached locally.
3) Attempts to call the admin-console or admin API return 401 (Unauthorized) or 403 (Forbidden) with token-binding mismatch messages in auth logs.
4) Restarting the customer's admin clients does not reliably fix; a restart of the auth-proxy pod temporarily restores admin access until next cert rotation or cache refresh window.
5) Customer attempted to re-run cert rotation twice and now cannot complete automation because the token validation step fails early in the pipeline.
logs: 2026-03-10T09:41:12Z auth-proxy[auth-1] WARN token_validation: token binding mismatch: presented_cert_thumbprint=3f:ab:2c..., token_cnf_claim=9e:dd:45...
2026-03-10T09:42:05Z auth-proxy[auth-1] INFO jwks_fetch: jwks last refreshed 2026-03-09T02:00:00Z
2026-03-10T09:42:07Z console[api] ERROR rbac: admin-lookup failed for subject=service-admin@finwave.example, reason=token-binding-verification-failed
comments: 2026-03-10 10:02 - Support (Asha): Thanks for the report. Can you confirm whether the IdP rotation changed only the certificate or also the client_id/secret? Also please provide a sample redacted token and the thumbprint of the new cert.
2026-03-10 11:12 - Customer (FinWave, J. Morales): We rotated only the cert. New thumbprint is 9e:dd:45:11:bf:2c. Attached a stripped token and the registration metadata from the enterprise app.

2026-03-10 14:25 - Support (Marcus): We can reproduce token-binding mismatch locally when auth-proxy has stale cert-thumbprint in cache. Tentative workaround: restart auth-proxy pod to force JWKS/cert-binding cache refresh. Will escalate to infra to investigate cache invalidation timing.

2026-03-11 09:03 - Engineering (Diego Ramos): Investigating auth-proxy cache codepath. Found that cert-thumbprint-to-client mapping is read from a long-lived cache (TTL 24h) and is not invalidated on JWKS refresh. Creating a patch to eagerly re-validate 'cnf' thumbprint on JWKS rotation.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: auth-proxy compares presented cert thumbprint against a cached 'known' thumbprint derived from a previous token exchange and doesn't pick up IdP-side rotation immediately.
Reproduction steps executed in staging with FinWave token: reproduced 401 with mismatched thumbprints when cache had stale value.

Observations: jwks fetch is occurring independently, but cert-thumbprint mapping is stored in an LRU cache keyed by client_id with TTL 24h. When IdP rotates certs, some callers present certs signed by the new key while cache still holds the old mapping for a day.
Auth-proxy log lines show explicit mismatch rather than missing claim, confirming binding validation code is running but against an outdated reference.
Workaround validated: restarting auth-proxy forces fresh mapping lookup and resolves the mismatch until TTL would otherwise refresh.
resolution: Workaround: Recommend customer restart auth-proxy pod(s) in their private deployment to force immediate refresh of certificate-thumbprint mapping (validated). Short-term fix deployed to customer's staging: reduce cache TTL to 5m pending permanent fix.
next_steps: 1) Engineering PR to change auth-proxy cache behavior: on JWKS rotation or explicit JWKS refresh, invalidate cert-thumbprint entries for matched client_ids (INT-3912).
2) Add monitoring alert for repeated token-binding-mismatch counts > 5/min (observable rule).
3) Release patch to all private customers in maintenance window; notify affected customers with remediation steps and recommended pre-rotation checks.
4) Follow-up runbook update: include explicit post-cert-rotation validation step and temporary pod restart guidance.
